AC-001.notes: Organisation and consent-review permissions, evidence, restrictions, expiry and independent review are individually enforced. No single authorised-user workflow test composes organisation creation through a recorded approved consent review.

AC-002.notes: Secure protected staging, source lineage, validation issues and reconciliation are tested, including streaming XLSX parsing. No single genuinely large contact-file acceptance run composes secure upload, validation, merge and reconciliation end to end.

AC-003.notes: PostgreSQL encryption/HMAC dedup, API masking and log/metric redaction are directly evidenced. Production frontend/UI masking remains deferred.

AC-004.notes: The cohort compiler directly builds NG/Lagos reported-age 18-35 selection with consent eligibility. The configured self-declared-age policy/staleness model required by the acceptance sentence is not fully implemented.

AC-005.notes: Final eligibility directly enforces active matching organisation/purpose/channel consent, expiry/withdrawal, suppression, contact state and governed frequency-cap policy at release/dispatch boundaries.

AC-006.notes: PostgreSQL rejects audience-snapshot mutation/deletion, and snapshot/materialisation evidence carries definition, consent-policy and configuration versions used for the campaign.

AC-007.notes: Message/media versioning, malware-clean trusted assets, controlled test sends and maker-checker approvals are individually tested. No single message+media workflow composes scan, test send and final maker-checker approval end to end.

AC-008.notes: PostgreSQL release rejects entitlement overflow transactionally with zero recipient/outbox rows; replay keeps exactly one recipient/outbox, and entitlement cannot be reused by another campaign.

AC-009.notes: Recipient ledger and transactional outbox remain atomic. Campaign-worker continuously runs PostgreSQL queue repair; exact PostgreSQL evidence deletes a durable dispatch job after its authoritative outbox event is already PUBLISHED and reconstructs exactly one job with the original deduplication key, while replay creates zero duplicates.

AC-010.notes: Accepted lease tranche ee79e82 proves exclusive current-process ownership and durable idempotency at the gateway submission boundary. Exact Linux tests cover boot ownership, heartbeat, authority, fsync/durability and provider-send fencing; PostgreSQL routing rejects stale-boot authority.

AC-011.notes: Crash reclaim, job deduplication and final eligibility remain enforced. Exact PostgreSQL queue-loss recovery reconstructs eligible missing obligations once, while UNKNOWN recipients are never reconstructed or resent; only an explicitly retryable state becomes repairable.

AC-012.notes: Migration 0092 and delivery metric transitions expose GATEWAY_ACCEPTED separately from SUBMITTING/SENT/DELIVERED/READ/FAILED/UNKNOWN. Exact PostgreSQL evidence proves gateway acceptance increments only gateway_accepted_total and exact replay is idempotent; campaign, organisation, pool and financial reporting consume the distinct metric.

AC-013.notes: Post-snapshot opt-out fails final dispatch eligibility and production PostgreSQL commits the suppression, append-only consent event and suppression-keyed campaign opt-out event in one transaction. Reporting derives campaign and organisation opt-out counts directly from that durable event ledger, so a locked or unavailable shared campaign_metrics counter cannot roll back or hide a legitimate STOP. Fresh PostgreSQL RED-to-GREEN evidence proves the former counter-coupled path timed out under a locked campaign_metrics row, while the final path commits the opt-out, remains replay-safe, and reports optOuts=1 exactly once on both report surfaces.

AC-014.notes: The synthetic five-million release test proves bounded 5,000-recipient batches and bounded sharding, but it does not create/resume/query/report a real persisted five-million-recipient ledger or measure the full acceptance workload.

AC-015.notes: Ten-million synthetic query benchmarking exists outside the repo and the production schema/compiler has high-volume indexes and bounded materialisation. The complete governed cohort path has not been benchmarked against ten million canonical contacts within accepted performance.

AC-016.notes: Production deployment/monitoring/backup design exists, but the acceptance truth requires a real Hostinger pilot plus successful backup/restore exercise. That external environment evidence does not yet exist.

AC-017.notes: Fresh security suites prove role/permission isolation, MFA/step-up, malware-safe uploads, PII/secret log redaction and permission+MFA+maker-checker protection for exports.

AC-018.notes: Append-only/audited evidence exists at consent, audience/import, campaign, execution/delivery and reporting stages, but there is no single acceptance test that reconstructs one complete chain from consent review through final report.

AC-019.notes: MIT attribution is retained and CI runs on pull requests/pushes; no upstream auto-merge workflow was found. This checkout origin is a local bundle, so hosted private-repository branch protection/direct-main blocking cannot be verified here.

AC-020.notes: Emergency/governance, incident/operations and capacity-representation controls exist in software, but formal operational-owner approval of runbooks, emergency stop and incident/capacity procedures remains an external readiness gate.

ADM-001.notes: The internal configuration catalogue enforces key/scope rules, canonical JSON, checksums, lifecycle and consumer-specific safety validation, but it has no first-class per-key typed schema/value-type registry; generic valid JSON is therefore broader than the SRS typed-catalogue requirement.

ADM-002.notes: PostgreSQL configuration versions are effective-dated and resolve deterministically; audience/routing/provider evidence freezes material versions. However campaigns.configuration_versions exists in schema but the active campaign model/repository does not read or write that generic field, so the exact campaign-record acceptance is not fully met.

ADM-003.notes: Release-one backend-freeze decision keeps retry/reconciliation/UNKNOWN settings as bounded deployment configuration under production change control. Consolidating them into one effective-dated maker-checker runtime policy remains a later governance refinement; the row remains PARTIAL by design.

ADM-004.notes: Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves approved effective-dated replacement plus rollback creates a new governed version, requires independent approval, preserves rollback/supersession evidence and resolves the prior value deterministically at the rollback effective time.

ADM-005.notes: Consent purposes/channels are data-driven rows and campaigns/imports enforce their linked consent review, so adding purpose data does not require a code constant. There is no complete governed purpose-administration service/API covering purpose, channel, expiry and review-rule configuration end to end.

ADM-006.notes: No governed age-estimation/staleness policy exists and the segment engine does not resolve an active age-policy version. Current logic uses self-declared reported age/recorded date only.

ADM-007.notes: State/LGA validation and stable reference codes exist, including rejection of invalid relationships, but the active geography catalogue is effectively seeded/read-only and no governed reference-data update workflow proves historical-code preservation after administrator changes.

ADM-008.notes: Versioned effective-dated maker-checker STOP keyword policy is configurable and re-testable; suppression/withdrawal precedence is enforced again at the final PostgreSQL eligibility boundary.

ADM-009.notes: Governed organisation/purpose/channel frequency-cap policy is effective-dated and eligibility/final dispatch enforce the active cap.

ADM-010.notes: Campaign approval has RBAC, fixed staged transitions and four-eyes final approval, but there is no governed configurable threshold/risk/category-to-role engine; changing the approval workflow still requires code/deployment.

ADM-011.notes: Sender/session rate, concurrency, allowance, cooldown/recovery and health thresholds are governed/versioned. Fresh PostgreSQL evidence proves the worker pacing controller resolves the approved policy and persists the exact policy ID/version into sender_pacing_runtime.

ADM-012.notes: Release-one backend-freeze decision accepts the proven bounded/configurable retry, reconciliation and UNKNOWN windows for launch. Moving those settings into one approved effective-dated platform-policy record remains a later governance refinement; the row remains PARTIAL by design.

ADM-013.notes: Reporting privacy thresholds and retention are governed/versioned and report outputs carry privacy policy evidence, but administrator-defined/versioned report-template composition is not implemented end to end.

ADM-014.notes: Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves business/security audit events are appended and ordinary UPDATE/DELETE attempts are rejected by database triggers.

ADM-015.notes: The audit model and PostgreSQL round-trip preserve actor, action, object, before/after, reason, IP/device, time and correlation ID when supplied, with a direct completeness test. Comprehensive proof that every applicable administrative/business path supplies all applicable context is still absent.

ADM-016.notes: Audit search supports actor/action/object/org/outcome/sensitivity/correlation/IP/time filters and controlled export, but there is no single composed acceptance test demonstrating an auditor can reconstruct one campaign end to end across consent, approval, dispatch and reporting.

ADM-017.notes: Audit storage is append-only, service-role access is explicit, and the persisted hash chain now canonicalises JSON/IP/timestamp representation. Fresh PostgreSQL verification passes and direct UPDATE/DELETE tampering is rejected.

ADM-018.notes: Governed operational alert policies, escalation and delivered portal notifications exist, but there is no dedicated signal/test proving privileged configuration changes or audit-integrity/control failures trigger an alert.

API-001.notes: The signed gateway delivery command contains only transport authority/routing evidence, recipient address, rendered approved message/media reference and correlation identifiers. A direct payload-inspection test captures the real HTTP command and rejects any field outside that transport set, including consent/suppression/demographic/attribute data.

API-002.notes: Recipient MSISDN remains encrypted in PostgreSQL until the campaign-worker material loader has loaded approved evidence, allocated a sender and validated the governed route. Decryption occurs immediately before send material construction. Production Compose grants the MSISDN encryption key to campaign-worker but not the OpenWA gateway, and the gateway payload carries only the resulting transport address; production-compose security validation passes.

API-003.notes: Control-plane route validation rejects paused/incompatible/stale session evidence and persists fenced authority. PostgreSQL acceptance proves conflicting cross-node authority is rejected/audited without replacing the owner, while the gateway authority check rejects stale/conflicting ownership before provider send.

API-004.notes: Durable gateway idempotency returns the original accepted provider result for repeated keys without another provider call, including after worker restart. Concurrent identical commands submit once; unresolved/UNKNOWN outcomes fail closed and are never auto-resubmitted.

API-005.notes: Gateway events carry stable eventId, control-plane clientReference and providerMessageId. The ingestor resolves deterministically by clientReference first or provider-message lookup when needed, persists provider correlation into delivery evidence, and binds eventId into replay/deduplication; tests prove both correlation modes plus conflicting event-ID replay rejection.

API-006.notes: Gateway capability/identity responses expose engine/adapter version and supported capabilities including message/event support. The control plane freezes the exact provider definition and blocks unsupported message types, engine/adapter versions and capability mismatches before dispatch.

API-007.notes: Service credentials are separated by purpose/service, production wiring uses mounted *_FILE secrets rather than committed values, gateway callback/command/runtime keys support bounded active+previous rotation with distinct strong secrets, and secret-file/production-compose validation passes. The committed-secret audit is also green.

API-008.notes: The control API is namespaced under /api/v1, internal gateway events carry explicit schemaVersion 1.0 and current contract/route tests run in CI. However there is no deployment/release gate comparing the current API/schema against a previously supported v1 consumer contract to detect breaking removals or incompatible changes, so backward compatibility within the major version is not fully proven.

APR-001.notes: A fixed approval sequence exists, but there is no configurable approval-stage engine selected by campaign risk, size or category.

APR-002.notes: Campaign progression cannot start audience build until consent approval, and the service validates the governed consent-review basis before approval.

APR-003.notes: The campaign state machine blocks commercial/final approval and dispatch while the submitted message remains unapproved; scheduling is reached only after message approval.

APR-004.notes: Final approval requires campaign.approve, recent MFA step-up at the HTTP handler, and an approver different from the campaign creator before the campaign becomes SCHEDULED.

APR-005.notes: Four-eyes rules exist for final campaign approval and commercial approval, but they are fixed rules rather than configuration/threshold-driven maker-checker policy.

APR-006.notes: Several approval domains record actor/reason/version and some have append-only events, but the complete campaign approval chain does not persist an immutable decision record with actor, time, comments and object version for every approval stage.

APR-007.notes: Material schedule, transport, audience, message or entitlement amendments regress campaign state and clear downstream approvals according to the changed evidence.

APR-008.notes: Commercial records capture quotation, invoice, payment and approval references through an offline governed workflow; no online payment mechanism is required.

APR-009.notes: A governed commercial approval can block progression, but the gate is mandatory in the fixed campaign workflow. No effective-dated policy switch was found to make payment/commercial blocking optional.

APR-010.notes: Campaign entitlement fields govern maximum unique recipients and messages per recipient. More than one message per recipient is rejected and PostgreSQL release rejects recipient-count overflow without leaking obligations.

APR-011.notes: PostgreSQL release proves the authorised obligation is bound to campaign, organisation, snapshot and message version; reuse with any mismatched binding is rejected.

APR-012.notes: Entitlement checking, recipient-ledger creation and outbox insertion occur in one PostgreSQL transaction. Concurrent releases at a one-recipient ceiling produce one success and one entitlement rejection with exactly one recipient/outbox row.

APR-013.notes: The current platform safely prohibits more than one message per recipient and binds release to the approved message version, but it has no workflow for obtaining a new approved entitlement for an additional message or resend outside policy.

APR-014.notes: EMERGENCY_STOP is an independently approved maintenance mode that blocks all governed actions and writes append-only maintenance lifecycle evidence. No direct integration was found that generates an operational alert when the emergency stop is activated.

APR-015.notes: No campaign/policy exception approval object was found that combines reason, expiry, independent second approval and report/audit visibility. Delivery reconciliation exceptions are a different workflow and do not satisfy this requirement.

BKP-001.notes: Scheduled PostgreSQL full backup/PITR/WAL archiving is a Railway production data-plane control. No production backup catalogue or recoverable chain exists yet; this is intentionally deferred to infrastructure integration.

BKP-002.notes: Independent-target backup encryption and key-controlled unreadability require the production backup destination/key-management design and live evidence; no such deployed backup exists in Task 5.

BKP-003.notes: Application database credentials are scoped and secret-file mounted, but a distinct production backup identity/credential set does not exist until the backup service is provisioned and access-reviewed.

BKP-004.notes: PostgreSQL retains object ownership/checksum/metadata while object bytes reside in private S3-compatible storage, but no independent object/evidence backup and restore exercise has yet restored bytes plus checksum under retention policy.

BKP-005.notes: Application deployment manifests, Dockerfiles and configuration are version-controlled in this repository and can reproduce the application topology. The required private hosted-repository assurance and a clean environment recreation exercise are not yet evidenced.

BKP-006.notes: The agreed production direction requires database-level recovery independent of VPS snapshots, but no production Railway database backup/restore evidence exists yet. Hostinger whole-VPS backup will not be accepted as the sole recovery mechanism.

BKP-007.notes: Monthly production restore testing cannot begin before the production backup chain exists. No signed restore-test report exists yet.

BKP-008.notes: General release/data integrity checks exist, but no automated post-restore validation currently proves restored row counts, cryptographic keys/object checksums and application compatibility because no production restore target is available yet.

BKP-009.notes: Replica promotion or recovery-target activation is provider/infrastructure work and has not been exercised against Railway/production PostgreSQL. RTO evidence is therefore unavailable.

BKP-010.notes: Backup immutability/versioning and ransomware separation depend on the selected independent backup target. No deployed policy/evidence exists yet.

BR-001.notes: A PostgreSQL release test gives a contact demographic age/gender values but removes consent; release produces zero obligations and a NO_ACTIVE_CONSENT exclusion. Demographic match alone cannot authorise communication.

BR-002.notes: Final eligibility directly rejects mismatched organisation, purpose or channel basis and independently rejects active suppression. Only the matching WhatsApp organisation/purpose basis with no overriding suppression remains eligible.

BR-003.notes: A queued recipient with previously active consent becomes ineligible immediately after the grant is WITHDRAWN; the final pre-send check returns CONSENT_WITHDRAWN before provider submission.

BR-004.notes: Natural-key/release replay and durable gateway idempotency prevent duplicate same-version submission, including concurrent calls and gateway restart. No separately approved resend workflow was found, so the explicit exception path in the rule is not implemented.

BR-005.notes: PostgreSQL rejects audience-snapshot UPDATE and DELETE. The additional rule that every changed audience must be materialised as a new snapshot and pass a new approval cycle is not yet directly proven end-to-end.

BR-006.notes: PostgreSQL rejects mutation of an approved message version; message-service evidence proves material body/variable/link/media changes create successive immutable versions with distinct hashes.

BR-007.notes: An approved entitlement for campaign A is rejected when campaign B attempts to validate/reuse it, while campaign A continues to validate the same approval.

BR-008.notes: The delivery state machine treats gateway acceptance, sent, delivered and read as distinct monotonic evidence states and does not infer later acknowledgements from earlier ones.

BR-009.notes: The platform has governed sender inventory and real OpenWA session plumbing, but acceptance requires proof against genuinely authenticated WhatsApp-registered MSISDN accounts. That is a live external gate, not something embedded tests can prove.

BR-010.notes: Campaigns use logical sender-pool abstractions for routing while the actual governed sender session remains internal execution evidence.

BR-011.notes: Accepted lease tranche ee79e82 establishes one active process owner per live WhatsApp session. PostgreSQL fencing, boot-bound signed heartbeat ownership and gateway process-local receipts jointly prevent stale owners from allocating, activating or submitting.

BR-012.notes: Governed stable per-session proxy routing exists and active-session proxy changes are rejected. Actual production worker/proxy IP stability and absence of rapid-rotation/evasion behaviour require deployed network evidence.

BR-013.notes: Admission uses live healthy-session safe MPM/daily capacity plus configured safety margin/headroom. Those safe-capacity values are supplied through governed session heartbeat state; no evidence yet proves they are derived from measured historical throughput rather than configured inputs.

BR-014.notes: The coordinator refuses campaign start when effective safe capacity cannot meet the hard deadline; admission returns REJECT/HOLD rather than silently accepting an infeasible deadline.

BR-015.notes: Ambiguous submission becomes UNKNOWN and durable gateway idempotency refuses an automatic replay. Reconciliation evidence is required before a resend-safe outcome can be established.

BR-016.notes: A real PostgreSQL governed profile conflict changes gender from MALE to FEMALE while the existing consent grant remains WITHDRAWN; no new or active consent grant is created.

BR-017.notes: Imported reported age is retained as supplied with source/recorded-at metadata and SELF_DECLARED_IMPORT evidence. No active derived estimated-age model or approximate-label contract exists, so the full rule is not closed.

BR-018.notes: No active inference engine was found, but there is also no governed approved-source/policy enforcement model for demographic or interest inference. Absence of inference is not sufficient evidence for this policy rule.

BR-019.notes: Recipient MSISDN is carried in the internal request body rather than the URL. Gateway durability tests prove MSISDN redaction from structured logs and prove Prometheus output for the static /v1/messages route contains no raw recipient MSISDN.

BR-020.notes: Release-one implementation exposes the internal administration application and internal-user authentication only; no external-organisation portal was found. A dedicated release-surface regression proving no client/self-service portal can be exposed has not yet been added, so this remains conservative.

BR-021.notes: Governed overrides/configurations carry reason, effective period, actor history and maker-checker approval. No explicit critical/high-risk override classification or additional second-approver requirement beyond the normal checker was found.

BR-022.notes: Campaign reports do not yet state complete metric definitions, denominators/formulas and provider-status limitations for every reported measure.

BR-023.notes: The PostgreSQL final eligibility check re-reads active suppressions immediately before submission; a queued recipient becomes ineligible with reason SUPPRESSED and the provider path is not authorised.

BR-024.notes: Authorised recipient obligations and durable jobs are PostgreSQL-backed rather than Redis-authoritative. A direct Redis-loss/recovery integration scenario has not yet been executed, so the explicit loss condition remains unclosed.

BR-025.notes: A submission crash/ambiguous provider error is recorded as UNKNOWN and durable idempotency blocks automatic re-submission until explicit reconciliation evidence exists.

BR-026.notes: Consent, audience snapshot, routing, provider capability, pacing, capacity and reporting-privacy versions are retained with campaign/execution evidence. The generic configuration catalogue is not yet automatically frozen into every consent, segmentation, dispatch and reporting decision.

BR-027.notes: Governed minimum cohort size is versioned/frozen into report evidence; PostgreSQL report proof suppresses all one-person demographic/geographic cells while leaving a cohort of two visible.

BR-028.notes: Approved effective-dated retention policies schedule/execute supported import-source, export-object and inbound-content actions with legal-hold/review controls. Full campaign media, provider-event and audit archival/deletion execution is not yet closed.

BR-029.notes: Suspended organisations fail closed for campaign progression/release, while quarantined sender sessions cannot be restored by heartbeat and contribute zero allocatable capacity.

BR-030.notes: Campaign transition requests require actor identity, material campaign changes have actor-attributed events, execution transitions have execution events, and sender governance changes are actor-attributed. Ordinary campaign approval-stage CompareAndSwap updates do not persist an equivalent actor-attributed status-history record, so every status change is not yet durably attributable.

CAM-001.notes: Campaigns require organisation and consent-review identifiers. Direct PostgreSQL release evidence proves a suspended organisation or rejected consent review blocks recipient release and creates no obligations.

CAM-002.notes: Campaign name, purpose, start window, completion deadline and creator identity are governed fields. A separate campaign category and distinct owner field are not present, so the full required metadata set is incomplete.

CAM-003.notes: The governed state machine implements Draft, approval stages, Scheduled, Dispatching, Paused, Completed, Completed With Exceptions and Cancelled with transition tests. There is no EXPIRED campaign status, so the required lifecycle is not complete.

CAM-004.notes: Campaign release binds an immutable snapshot and material changes invalidate approvals.

CAM-005.notes: Text, image+caption, video and document drafts are accepted with required clean media metadata. Immediately before dispatch each type maps to SEND_TEXT/SEND_IMAGE/SEND_VIDEO/SEND_DOCUMENT and both the frozen provider definition and assigned gateway pool must advertise that capability; missing capability is rejected.

CAM-006.notes: Assets use trusted server-derived checksum, content type, size and malware status; quarantined/revoked/tampered objects fail closed and storage supports filesystem or S3/MinIO.

CAM-007.notes: Variables are declared with governed data types and optional fallbacks. Preview resolves fallbacks and masks sensitive values, while dispatch mode fails closed when a required value is missing or a placeholder is undeclared.

CAM-008.notes: A preview endpoint renders the exact message template and masks sensitive values by default. Preview values are caller-supplied; no mechanism was found that selects representative approved test records, so the stated representative-record acceptance is not complete.

CAM-009.notes: Only maker-checker approved test MSISDNs may receive test sends. Test sends freeze the message content hash, explicit OpenWA engine, gateway pool, session, provider adapter and exact provider capability definition/version. Scheduling and worker execution revalidate required capabilities and fail closed on route drift; idempotent replay compares the frozen request.

CAM-010.notes: Message content is append-only by version rather than edited in place. A direct test changes body, variables, links and media across successive drafts, proves versions 1/2/3 with distinct stable hashes, and proves all historical versions remain retrievable.

CAM-011.notes: Approved message content has a deterministic SHA-256 content hash and the campaign aggregate exposes the hash from its frozen approved message version. PostgreSQL release rejects any message version different from the campaign-approved version before creating obligations, so dispatch recipients reference the exact immutable version.

CAM-012.notes: Material audience, message, entitlement, transport and schedule changes are explicit, MFA-protected, optimistically versioned, recorded append-only and automatically regress the campaign to the required approval stage.

CAM-013.notes: No governed campaign-type reply/STOP instruction policy with required-instruction validation is implemented.

CAM-014.notes: No controlled tracked-link redirect service with signed recipient-safe attribution is implemented.

CAM-015.notes: Destination links must use HTTPS and, when a governed host allow-list is configured, the destination hostname must be present. Tests prove both unsafe scheme and a valid HTTPS URL on an unapproved domain are blocked while an allow-listed HTTPS domain is accepted.

CAM-016.notes: Campaigns persist UTC start/deadline timestamps plus a declared IANA timezone, and timezone/quiet-hours validation exists. No acceptance-level DST scheduling test or local-time scheduling conversion proof was found, so timezone scheduling closure remains partial.

CAM-017.notes: Per-campaign quiet hours are validated in the campaign timezone and the final pre-send checker detects quiet hours. Organisation/jurisdiction sending-window composition is not implemented, and temporarily blocked queued work is currently suppressed rather than held for the next permitted window.

CAM-018.notes: Requested start and completion deadline are governed and capacity admission computes whether the deadline is achievable. No explicit latest-admission time field or policy exists anywhere in the active repository, so that required scheduling control is missing.

CAM-019.notes: Pause/resume/cancel are reasoned campaign transitions and final eligibility sees PAUSED state. Undispatched durable-job claims are not campaign-gated and paused queued work is terminally suppressed instead of held, so state changes do not yet have the required complete effect on undispatched jobs.

CAM-020.notes: The campaign workspace exposes cancellation impact before cancel, including outstanding, already-submitted/cannot-recall and UNKNOWN/reconciliation counts plus warnings. Equivalent impact calculation before audience invalidation is not evidenced.

CAM-021.notes: The control API exposes archive/restore for terminal campaigns and no campaign DELETE route was found. There is no direct destructive-delete rejection test tied to campaigns with audit or delivery history, so the acceptance is not promoted from API absence alone.

CAM-022.notes: Campaign tags and internal notes are persisted, notes are categorised, and workspace mutations are separated from client-facing campaign fields. There is no explicit note visibility classification or direct client-report leakage regression, so visibility controls are incomplete.

CAM-023.notes: Clone creates a fresh draft ID and strips frozen audience, approved message, commercial approval and final approval evidence. However the clone reuses the source maximum-recipient entitlement by default unless a new value is supplied, so the acceptance requirement that old entitlement cannot be reused is not fully satisfied.

CAM-024.notes: Terminal campaigns can be archived/restored with actor, reason, optimistic versioning and append-only workspace audit events while the underlying campaign/reportable data remains present. Archive timing is not driven by the governed retention-policy subsystem, so retention-policy archival is incomplete.

CNS-001.notes: Consent is a separate durable grant ledger; one contact is directly proven to hold multiple independent active consent scopes in PostgreSQL.

CNS-002.notes: Eligibility requires exact organisation/controller, purpose and channel scope; wrong organisation, purpose or channel is rejected in direct tests and at the final PostgreSQL send check.

CNS-003.notes: PostgreSQL round-trip proves grant/effective time, source type/reference, wording version, evidence object/checksum and creator evidence are retained.

CNS-004.notes: All required states exist and ineligible states are rejected by eligibility, but the active ledger service only provides first-class create/withdraw operations for grants; governed EXPIRED, REVOKED and SUPERSEDED transition workflows are not complete.

CNS-005.notes: Effective-from and expiry timestamps are stored and future/expired grants are directly rejected by eligibility.

CNS-006.notes: Withdrawal records actor/source/reason/time through append-only consent events and immediately makes the scoped grant ineligible, including at final dispatch.

CNS-007.notes: Latest effective event semantics make a later withdrawal override an older active grant; direct event-order tests pass.

CNS-008.notes: A later valid re-consent is a new grant with new evidence and later timestamp; the earlier withdrawn grant remains withdrawn and is not reactivated.

CNS-009.notes: Consent events are append-only in PostgreSQL; create/withdraw event history reconstructs the tested current state and database UPDATE/DELETE attempts are rejected.

CNS-010.notes: GLOBAL, ORGANISATION, PURPOSE and CHANNEL suppression scopes each exclude exactly the intended eligibility context; mismatched scope does not exclude.

CNS-011.notes: Signed inbound replies are resolved through the authoritative recipient relationship; a recognised STOP command creates an immediate idempotent global suppression under the active confirmation policy.

CNS-012.notes: STOP synonyms and language variants are governed through versioned effective-dated maker-checker policy and resolved at inbound execution time.

CNS-013.notes: Authorised manual suppression with reason is exposed by the consent HTTP workflow, writes SUPPRESSION_CREATED audit evidence and is immediately effective in eligibility.

CNS-014.notes: Real PostgreSQL erasure anonymises the profile while retaining the minimised lookup HMAC, creates one active GLOBAL suppression carrying that HMAC, and uniqueness prevents re-import as a second canonical contact.

CNS-015.notes: INVALID and RECYCLED lifecycle statuses can be assigned under authority, but no repeated-hard-failure automation or configured review/suppression trigger was found.

CNS-016.notes: Consent/suppression eligibility is compiled for estimate and materialisation/snapshot, while PostgreSQL final eligibility rechecks immediately before dispatch; withdrawal after snapshot is directly proven to hold the queued send.

CNS-017.notes: An approved consent-review basis does not override an individual withdrawal: the final PostgreSQL send check rejects the withdrawn grant while review approval remains present.

CNS-018.notes: Exact release exclusion reason_code values are durably stored and aggregated, but no authorised operations endpoint was found that displays per-contact exclusion reasons as required by the acceptance example.

CNS-019.notes: Per-grant expiry is implemented and snapshots record a consentPolicyVersion, but no governed configurable consent-expiry/renewal policy service was found behind that version.

CNS-020.notes: Privacy access/export packages include consent and suppression evidence, are encrypted and integrity-checked, log immutable export-request evidence, and the actual HTTP route requires privacy.read plus recent MFA step-up before export work.

CON-001.notes: Duplicate approved imports of the same protected E.164 resolve to one canonical contact. Identity is currently one platform-wide HMAC namespace; a governed configurable identity-scope model is not implemented.

CON-003.notes: PostgreSQL evidence proves the stored identifier is ciphertext, contains no plaintext MSISDN, and decrypts to the canonical E.164 value.

CON-004.notes: Keyed HMAC lookup is deterministic and the unique database lookup key resolves duplicate imports to the same canonical contact.

CON-005.notes: Backend/API masking is tested, but the production frontend is deferred, so the UI portion of the acceptance criterion has not been executed.

CON-006.notes: Plaintext decryption is constrained to final dispatch and approved privacy/export execution paths. Target-deployment least-privilege service/database identities still require environment evidence.

CON-007.notes: The real import validator rejects an invalid state/LGA relationship as INVALID_GEOGRAPHY; canonical merge resolves geography through controlled reference rows.

CON-008.notes: Missing optional state/LGA remains blank and is distinct from invalid geography. Import staging still requires/defaults a country ISO2, so fully unknown country is not yet represented.

CON-009.notes: The canonical-contact PostgreSQL test preserves the exact self-declared numeric age and its recorded date.

CON-010.notes: No configured estimated-current-age approximation model or birthday/partial-date boundary implementation was found.

CON-011.notes: Age source, verification flag and recorded date are stored. The segment builder does not expose confidence/source/verification filters and there is no confidence field or separate governed last-confirmed model.

CON-012.notes: Two imports update current reported age while retaining both old and new observations with source hashes in profile history.

CON-013.notes: No governed configurable age-staleness bands or segment-count acceptance test for changing a staleness threshold was found.

CON-014.notes: Gender is optional/self-declared and canonical merge requires an approved review/purpose basis; no inference implementation was found. Explicit per-attribute purpose governance and unknown-gender acceptance evidence remain incomplete.

CON-015.notes: The catalogue supports typed dynamic attributes, allowed values, permissions and safe segmentation queries. A governed end-to-end ingestion/write path for optional dynamic attributes such as interests is not yet evidenced.

CON-016.notes: Dynamic attribute values record source_system and recorded_at, but no confidence field/model exists and complete segmentation-attribute lineage is not proven end-to-end.

CON-017.notes: The lifecycle supports active, inactive, invalid, recycled, deceased and additional terminal/suppressed states; final dispatch rejects every contact whose status is not ACTIVE.

CON-018.notes: The PostgreSQL merge test traces one canonical contact through two source systems/import batches with two durable source links and source-record hashes.

CON-019.notes: Approved import dedup/update is governed and import mutations are captured for controlled rollback, but there is no explicit canonical-contact-to-contact merge workflow proving preservation of two existing contacts consent and event lineage.

CON-020.notes: Ordinary contact operations use opaque contact IDs. Permission-guarded privacy workflows require a complete exact E.164 value before HMAC lookup; a partial plaintext MSISDN is rejected.

CON-021.notes: PostgreSQL rectification changes the current profile while preserving the old profile with privacy-case ID, executor, reason and original source-system/source-record lineage.

CON-022.notes: High-volume indexes and asynchronous audience materialisation avoid a schema redesign path, but no genuine 10-million-canonical-contact NFR load test has been executed.

CRV-001.notes: Consent review explicitly supports ORGANISATION, SOURCE and CAMPAIGN scope with scope-specific validation. PostgreSQL lifecycle acceptance proves a SOURCE-scoped review persists its source identity and governance evidence.

CRV-002.notes: Collection method, source system, consent source and collection date range are persisted, and SOURCE scope requires sourceSystem. Submission requires collectionMethod and consentSource. There is no distinct URL/form-identifier field, and sourceSystem is not mandatory for organisation/campaign-scoped reviews, so the exact provenance requirement is not fully enforced.

CRV-003.notes: Submission requires both wordingVersion and exactConsentWording; both persist with an approved review. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance reads them back and revision evidence proves changed wording creates a new governed review.

CRV-004.notes: Organisation, controller role, purpose code, channel, campaign scope and permitted partner organisations are stored. Campaign eligibility enforces organisation, channel, expiry and campaign-specific scope, but does not currently compare campaign purpose against review purposeCode or enforce permittedPartnerOrganisations for organisation/source-scoped reuse.

CRV-005.notes: Reviews accept governed evidence assets and external evidence references carrying SHA-256 checksums; malformed or non-lowercase checksums are rejected and approved evidence references persist with the review.

CRV-006.notes: Uploaded consent evidence resolves only through the trusted-asset path, which requires CLEAN malware-scan state before evidence becomes usable by a review. Existing HTTP/service acceptance exercises trusted evidence resolution.

CRV-007.notes: Independent decision records reviewer, reviewedAt, outcome, expiry, next-review time, restrictions and reason. Approval requires a future expiry; fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves an attributable time-bounded approved-with-restrictions decision survives persistence.

CRV-008.notes: Approved, approved-with-restrictions, rejected, revoked and superseded transitions are governed and append-only audited. EXPIRED is a valid schema/event state and expiry is enforced dynamically, but no runtime transition was found that moves an approved row to EXPIRED and emits the EXPIRED event.

CRV-009.notes: Decision reason is mandatory for approval/rejection, approved-with-restrictions additionally requires explicit restriction text, and revocation requires a longer reason. Blank/short reasons are rejected by the domain rules; PostgreSQL acceptance proves restriction and revocation reasons persist.

CRV-010.notes: Sample review notes are bounded and reject email-address and phone-number patterns; approval can record sampled-record review evidence without retaining unnecessary direct sample PII.

CRV-011.notes: Approved review fields have no mutable edit endpoint. Material changes use the revision workflow: a replacement review is created, the prior review becomes SUPERSEDED and ineligible, and the replacement must be submitted and independently approved. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves lineage, supersession events and reapproval after wording change.

CRV-012.notes: Campaign progression/release requires a valid linked consent review and PostgreSQL release evidence rejects invalid review status/expiry. The SRS also permits a separately approved non-consent lawful-basis alternative; no such governed alternative workflow was found.

CRV-013.notes: Expired review approval is blocked by campaign eligibility/release and fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves an approved review becomes ineligible after expiresAt. No dedicated advance-expiry warning/alert path was found, so the warning half of the acceptance remains open.

CRV-014.notes: No authorised compliance override for consent-review eligibility with reason, expiry and independent second approval was found. Existing consent-review revocation requires step-up MFA but is not an eligibility override.

DLV-001.notes: PostgreSQL enforces UNIQUE(campaign_id, contact_id, message_version_id). A database-backed release/replay test proves the same release creates exactly one authoritative recipient natural key and one associated outbox row.

DLV-003.notes: Recipient authorisation and transactional-outbox creation run in one serializable PostgreSQL transaction. An entitlement-overflow integration test proves an error after attempted recipient creation rolls the whole transaction back to zero recipient and zero outbox rows.

DLV-004.notes: A PostgreSQL crash-recovery test leaves an outbox row leased by publisher A, reclaims it with publisher B after lease expiry, advances the fence, safely replays publication, creates exactly one durable job, and completes the outbox as PUBLISHED.

DLV-005.notes: Campaign recipients and transactional outbox remain authoritative in PostgreSQL and queue publication is replay-safe while the outbox is pending/processing. There is no mechanism to reconstruct a durable job that is lost after its outbox record is already PUBLISHED, so complete queue rebuild from authoritative eligible state is not proven.

DLV-006.notes: An explicit five-million-recipient test completes as 1,000 bounded release calls of at most 5,000 recipients each. Deterministic sharding with a 10,000-recipient target remains within 500 shards rather than creating one unbounded transaction or job.

DLV-007.notes: Real PostgreSQL FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED claiming gives exactly one concurrent owner. After lease expiry a second worker reclaims the job with an advanced fence, and the stale owner cannot complete it.

DLV-008.notes: PostgreSQL allocation assigns only a fresh READY/capable sender. The integration test proves stale worker heartbeat, exhausted daily sender capacity, and expired sender lease each result in ErrNoHealthySession.

DLV-009.notes: The final pre-send PostgreSQL check correctly detects PAUSED, future-start, deadline-passed and quiet-hours states before gateway submission. However the dispatch handler currently converts every ineligible decision into SUPPRESSED_BEFORE_SEND, so temporary schedule/pause holds become terminal suppression instead of remaining held for later dispatch.

DLV-010.notes: Immediately before submission the authoritative PostgreSQL checker re-reads contact status, suppressions and current consent. Integration evidence proves inactive contact, global suppression and consent withdrawal are excluded, while the handler test proves an excluded recipient never reaches the gateway.

DLV-011.notes: Per-sender governed pacing, hourly/daily allowances, active-campaign limits, message-type overrides and in-flight constraints exist. No acceptance-level load test demonstrates bounded throughput under sustained load, so the stated acceptance is not yet proven.

DLV-012.notes: A PostgreSQL retry-history test executes two submission attempts and proves all six ordered delivery events remain in delivery_events while the authoritative recipient ends at GATEWAY_ACCEPTED with AttemptCount=2.

DLV-013.notes: Gateway failures are classified SAFE_TO_RETRY, PERMANENT or OUTCOME_UNKNOWN. Durable retries support validated failure-code category overrides for base/max delay and jitter; OUTCOME_UNKNOWN cannot be configured as retryable and is explicitly forced out of automatic retry. Category policy is deployment-configurable with fail-closed parsing.

DLV-014.notes: Durable retries now use governed bounded exponential delay with configurable base/max values and deterministic per-job/attempt jitter. Configuration validation caps invalid/unbounded settings, and OUTCOME_UNKNOWN is explicitly excluded from the automatic retry path.

DLV-015.notes: Uncertain outcomes remain reconciliation-required and can only be resolved through an MFA-protected, evidence-backed operator action; confirmed non-submission is blocked when provider evidence exists.

DLV-016.notes: CONFIRM_NOT_SUBMITTED rejects provider correlation/acknowledgement evidence, requires an explicit duplicateRiskAccepted acknowledgement, exposes POSSIBLE_DUPLICATE_SEND risk to the operator, and records governed reconciliation evidence/audit. Automatic UNKNOWN remains sticky and never auto-resends; only explicit reviewed CONFIRM_NOT_SUBMITTED evidence authorises the recipient to transition to FAILED_RETRYABLE for governed retry.

DLV-017.notes: Campaign pause/resume is governed and audited, final eligibility remains fail-closed, and PostgreSQL job claiming now excludes DISPATCH_CAMPAIGN_RECIPIENT work unless the authoritative recipient belongs to a DISPATCHING campaign. The acceptance test proves a PAUSED job stays PENDING with attempt_count unchanged and becomes claimable once the campaign resumes.

DLV-018.notes: Campaign cancellation now atomically marks only undispatched AUTHORIZED/QUEUED/CLAIMED/FAILED_RETRYABLE obligations CANCELLED inside the serializable lifecycle transaction, preserves attempt counts, records immutable cancellation evidence, cancels still-pending dispatch jobs and reconciles aggregate counters. UNKNOWN and provider-accepted outcomes remain unchanged.

DLV-019.notes: A subprocess worker-kill acceptance test proves a separately running worker can claim then exit without completion; after lease expiry exactly one replacement worker reclaims the same obligation, attempt_count and lease_version advance monotonically, and the dead owner is fenced from completion.

DLV-020.notes: The campaign worker continuously runs PostgreSQL queue repair. An explicit queue-loss test deletes a durable dispatch job after its authoritative outbox event is already PUBLISHED and proves exactly one job is reconstructed with the original deduplication key; a second repair creates zero. UNKNOWN/terminal recipients are not reconstructed.

DLV-021.notes: Operations exposes global queue depth and oldest queued timestamp and supports governed queue-depth alerting. The required queue depth/oldest-job dimensions by campaign, shard and sender are not exposed, so the dashboard/alert acceptance is only partial.

DLV-022.notes: Durable jobs carry a numeric priority and claims order higher priority first. There is no governed configurable campaign-priority policy and no fairness/starvation acceptance test proving normal campaigns continue to progress.

DLV-023.notes: Explicit approved routing plans create visible HELD/ACTIVE/RELEASED per-pool capacity reservations with rate/hourly/daily units and fencing. No high-priority-only policy binding or reservation-specific append-only audit trail was found; routing-plan approval metadata alone does not fully prove the reservation audit acceptance.

DLV-024.notes: Forecast recomputes remaining work and measured available capacity on every assessment. A direct coordinator test proves reducing measured throughput from 20 to 10 messages/minute moves projected completion later and updates the effective-throughput evidence.

DLV-025.notes: Admission compares required rate/volume against measured rate and daily capacity with a safety margin and returns ADMIT/HOLD/REJECT with reasons. PostgreSQL evidence proves the capacity reference, evidence version, remaining volume, measured capacity, safety margin, required/effective rate, forecast, deadline, decision, reasons and evaluation time are durably recorded.

EVT-001.notes: Gateway delivery and inbound callbacks are authenticated over exact body bytes with HMAC, bounded timestamp validation and dual-key rotation support; invalid signatures are rejected. No dedicated security alert/audit path for an invalid gateway signature was found, so the acceptance requirement that rejection is also alerted is not fully closed.

EVT-002.notes: The versioned callback contract requires eventId, supported eventType and occurredAt, and requires providerMessageId for acknowledgement states while allowing a safe clientReference fallback. Unknown fields, missing identifiers and weak evidence are rejected with 400/422 responses, but malformed provider events are not durably quarantined for later review.

EVT-003.notes: PostgreSQL enforces one durable event per deduplication key and binds the key to an immutable fingerprint. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves replay of the same provider event does not create another event or increment campaign metrics twice, while conflicting reuse is rejected.

EVT-004.notes: The delivery reducer uses monotonic acknowledgement precedence and preserves each accepted event in delivery_events. State-machine acceptance proves delivered-before-sent remains DELIVERED, and PostgreSQL acceptance proves the durable event history is retained.

EVT-005.notes: Delivery events retain minimised provider event/message identifiers, canonical type/time and bounded error metadata, with time-key indexing/partition-readiness for retention operations. The system does not preserve a separately redacted raw provider envelope and exposes no dedicated authorised diagnostic event-inspection surface governed by an event-retention policy.

EVT-006.notes: Known OpenWA sent/ack/delivered/read/failed states are normalised into the canonical gateway event contract and bounded canonical error codes. Direct contract coverage for the provider-specific mapping table/reason taxonomy is incomplete, and current OpenWA failure mapping is coarse rather than a fully governed retryable/permanent reason catalogue.

EVT-007.notes: Authenticated gateway events correlate by clientReference/providerMessageId; unresolved events are durably recorded in the PostgreSQL unmatched-event reconciliation queue with provider-event deduplication, while the control plane returns retryable GATEWAY_EVENT_DEFERRED so the gateway durable outbox retries the exact same event until correlation is available. Once correlated, the queued unmatched record is resolved. Memory runtime has equivalent bounded test semantics.

EVT-008.notes: State-machine tests prove lower-confidence late progress/ack/failure events cannot downgrade stronger SENT/DELIVERED/READ evidence. Contradictory late evidence is retained as reconciliation-required instead of rewriting the higher-confidence state.

EVT-009.notes: Authenticated inbound messages are checked synchronously against the governed opt-out keyword policy. The signed inbound STOP acceptance test proves suppression is created idempotently before the callback returns, while a non-command does not suppress.

EVT-010.notes: Inbound replies are encrypted at rest, content reveal uses a separate inbound.content.read permission and audited reveal path, retention redacts plaintext while preserving minimised fingerprint/operational evidence, and legal hold prevents premature content deletion.

EVT-011.notes: Authorised inbound.review users can classify QUESTION/COMPLAINT/OPT_OUT/OTHER, mark escalation, require an escalation reason, and persist reviewer/time/version evidence. The review/classification mutation does not append a dedicated immutable audit event, so the acceptance that the action is audited is not fully met.

EVT-012.notes: Release-one backend-freeze decision retains scheduled stale-submission/UNKNOWN reconciliation, configured aging and governed manual evidence resolution, while deferring transport-specific provider polling until a reliable provider API and evidenced release need exist. The row remains PARTIAL by design and is not a release-one backend blocker.

EVT-013.notes: Release-one backend-freeze decision retains sticky UNKNOWN plus configured final-UNKNOWN aging/evidence without introducing a second recipient status taxonomy. The internal operator console will surface reconciliation age/evidence; the row remains PARTIAL by design and is not a release-one backend blocker.

EVT-014.notes: Recipients preserve highestAcknowledgement, contradiction count and reconciliation-required evidence when later outcomes conflict with earlier gateway/provider acknowledgement. Campaign metrics expose Submitted/Sent/Delivered/Read/Failed/Unknown funnel stages, but GATEWAY_ACCEPTED is folded into Submitted and there is no distinct acceptance-versus-later-outcome discrepancy metric.

EVT-015.notes: No first-party asynchronous bulk provider-status import/reconciliation adapter contract was found. Current status ingestion is callback/event based plus governed manual exception resolution.

GWY-001.notes: The consolidated worker exposes a versioned /v1 internal contract over MessagingProvider rather than the upstream OpenWA public API. OpenWAProvider delegates that contract directly to the embedded engine, and the embedded provider/lifecycle contract test plus the production Docker build verify the interface.

GWY-002.notes: Every send requires a validated idempotency key. Durable pre-submit evidence survives restart; concurrent/replayed duplicates return the original provider outcome without another provider call, while unresolved or UNKNOWN outcomes are never submitted again automatically.

GWY-003.notes: A PostgreSQL concurrency test proves only one worker acquires a live session lease and stale ownership is fenced after takeover. The gateway separately persists and validates session authority so stale/conflicting owners are rejected before provider send.

GWY-004.notes: Engine authentication/session directories are wired to persistent worker storage, but the acceptance truth requires an encrypted production worker volume and a genuine authenticated WhatsApp restart proving restoration without re-pairing where the engine permits. That Hostinger/live-provider evidence is not yet available.

GWY-005.notes: Signed runtime registration reports heartbeat/build/runtime identity, capacity, session count, queue depth, CPU, memory, disk, inode, process/file-descriptor and network evidence. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves the governed stale threshold marks only expired nodes unavailable.

GWY-006.notes: Signed per-session heartbeat propagates current gateway lifecycle state into governed sender_sessions and the operations dashboard. Exact PostgreSQL evidence drives READY -> DISCONNECTED -> CONNECTING -> READY through signed heartbeats and proves dashboard state plus unhealthy-session counts follow the transitions.

GWY-007.notes: Dispatch persists a fenced session authority before sending and now appends an immutable REJECTED event when a stale/conflicting cross-node owner loses the authority upsert. PostgreSQL acceptance proves the live owner is unchanged and the rejection is audited; gateway fencing proves the rejected owner cannot reach provider send.

GWY-008.notes: Each session has its own bounded pipeline with configurable in-flight and waiter limits. A direct load acceptance runs 30 operations against one session with SESSION_IN_FLIGHT_LIMIT=3 and observes a maximum of exactly 3 concurrent operations with the queue draining to zero.

GWY-009.notes: Governed node/session draining blocks new work while the gateway pipeline rejects queued/new operations after drain and lets already-active operations finish through their normal idempotent outcome path. Control-plane maintenance/drain state prevents unsafe new campaign/session work.

GWY-010.notes: Provider message identifiers are returned by the gateway, carried on canonical events and persisted into recipient/attempt history. Provider status is normalised into canonical event/error fields; there is no separately persisted redacted raw-provider-status metadata object, so the exact metadata portion remains incomplete.

GWY-011.notes: Delivery/read and inbound events are durably queued by the gateway and forwarded through signed callbacks. The control plane verifies signatures, replay windows and event identity; forged/replayed callbacks are rejected. Genuine WhatsApp callback shapes remain a separate live validation gate, not a reason to weaken this code-side acceptance.

GWY-012.notes: The worker has no campaign-audience repository. Durable send idempotency stores fingerprints/outcomes rather than recipient/body/route payloads and is capped; the acceptance test explicitly proves those raw send fields are absent from persisted idempotency evidence. Local outboxes contain individual transport events and session storage contains engine/session state, not audience lists.

GWY-013.notes: Messages freeze trusted object references, media type/size/checksum and route capability evidence. Dispatch resolves bounded object access per recipient and enforces the frozen provider attachment ceiling rather than materialising a campaign media batch in worker memory.

GWY-014.notes: The gateway uses a sanitising JSON logger and static-safe metrics. Automated durability/log tests prove raw MSISDN, QR/pairing material, session token, message content and credential-bearing DSN fragments are removed from logs/metrics.

GWY-015.notes: Shutdown hooks and durable outboxes preserve pending event work. A real child-process kill during provider submission now proves that restart converts crash-left PENDING submission evidence to UNKNOWN and the same idempotency key cannot automatically reach the provider again.

GWY-016.notes: The control plane governs provider/engine capability and version definitions, freezes the exact binding into campaign/test-send evidence and blocks incompatible gateway, adapter, minimum-version or message-capability routes. The worker exposes its runtime identity/capabilities under the versioned internal API.

GWY-017.notes: Per-session stable proxy configuration is encrypted/audited in PostgreSQL, requires privileged recent-MFA administration, cannot change while the session is active, and reaches both embedded engine shapes without persisting worker credentials. The remaining acceptance is an actual connectivity/egress test through the approved production proxy, which requires deployed Hostinger/network evidence.

GWY-018.notes: First-party proxy behavior is explicitly stable-session routing only: active-session changes are rejected, restart does not silently reuse prior proxy authority, and source review found no rotation scheduler, pool cycling or enforcement-evasion path. The approved runtime-governance design also explicitly prohibits rapid rotation/evasion.

HST-001.notes: Production Compose publishes no application host ports and places first-party services on an internal private network; the historical reverse-proxy config limits portal/API/health paths. Actual Railway/Hostinger TLS termination and an external port scan against the production endpoints are deferred to infrastructure integration.

HST-002.notes: SSH source allowlisting, VPN/key-only access and unauthorised-source connection testing are Hostinger/production-host controls. No deployed production host is available in Task 5, so this remains an explicit infrastructure gate.

HST-003.notes: The first-party production stack uses an internal network and does not publish PostgreSQL or Redis ports; the agreed Railway architecture also keeps managed data services private. The acceptance requires real production firewall/external-scan evidence, which is deferred.

HST-004.notes: Control/gateway commands, callbacks and runtime reports are signed, replay-resistant and bound to governed node identities; production Compose isolates service traffic. Cross-provider firewall/static-egress and optional mTLS evidence require the Railway/Hostinger deployment.

HST-005.notes: Service/object-store/gateway endpoints are parameterised by DNS/service URL rather than hardcoded production IPs, preserving provider portability. A real DNS/certificate move and migration exercise has not yet been performed.

HST-006.notes: Signed command/callback/runtime contracts enforce bounded timestamp skew, but secure NTP/time-synchronisation is a node/hosting control. Clock-drift evidence across Railway and Hostinger nodes requires the production infrastructure phase.

HST-007.notes: Gateway runtime inventory persists governed node ID, pool/provider/engine, adapter/gateway/worker/config versions, internal URL, boot ID, capabilities, state, capacity and resource telemetry. It does not provide a complete CMDB record of host OS, public/private IP and infrastructure role for every production node.

HST-008.notes: Application maintenance/drain controls can stop unsafe new work and gracefully drain active gateway operations, but OS/container patch execution evidence and a tested host rollback procedure require deployed Railway/Hostinger environments.

HST-009.notes: Production services use distinct mounted secret files and scoped database identities, and active/smoke development gateway identities are separated. A production/staging/monitoring credential inventory and access review across the deployed providers has not yet been executed.

HST-010.notes: Runtime telemetry now covers CPU, memory, disk bytes, inode counts, PID/uptime, file descriptors and network RX/TX/interface count, and governed operational alerts cover node/session health and backlog. Alert policies do not yet expose dedicated disk/inode/PID/network threshold metrics and no production failure simulation has demonstrated notification delivery.

IAM-001.notes: Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves an administrator-provisioned internal account can authenticate while an unprovisioned identity is rejected with invalid credentials; no self-registration path exists.

IAM-002.notes: MFA challenge/verification and persistent MFA sessions are directly proven, and provisioning/reset default to MFA. However account administration can set MFARequired=false and the login service permits first-factor-only sessions for such accounts, so the unconditional mandatory-MFA acceptance is not fully enforced.

IAM-003.notes: No real pluggable OIDC/SAML/passwordless identity-provider abstraction/configuration was found; current authentication is internal password + TOTP.

IAM-004.notes: Ordinary application routes are wrapped in RBAC permission middleware and targeted permission-denial tests exist, but there is no exhaustive permission-matrix acceptance covering every protected action with its exact expected permission.

IAM-005.notes: Fresh PostgreSQL evidence proves one user can hold multiple roles and receives the least-privilege permission union (campaign.write + finance.write). The current /auth/me JSON deliberately omits the effective permissions map, so the acceptance-required display of effective permissions is incomplete.

IAM-006.notes: Final campaign approval/release uses campaign.approve authorization plus four-eyes actor separation; creator/self-approver paths are rejected where maker-checker is required.

IAM-007.notes: Fresh MFA step-up is enforced across exports, privacy/legal-hold actions, identity administration, platform-policy changes, campaign final approval/release, execution controls and destructive/import operations. A dedicated cryptographic-key-change/rotation action with step-up evidence is not implemented, so the full named scope is not closed.

IAM-008.notes: Idle and absolute session timeouts are deployment-configurable, validated and wired into both memory and PostgreSQL runtimes; expired/revoked sessions are rejected by Authenticate before protected APIs execute.

IAM-009.notes: Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves administrator disable immediately revokes an existing live session and the revoked token cannot authenticate; credential reset and lock/unlock operations also revoke/reset access state.

IAM-010.notes: Persistent failed-login counting and threshold lockout are now directly proven, including five bad attempts causing a timed lock. The threshold and lock duration remain hard-coded at 5 attempts/15 minutes rather than governed configurable controls.

IAM-011.notes: Authentication success/failure, MFA, lockout, permission/step-up/network-denied events are persisted with actor/time/context, and privileged business actions use the audit ledger. Authentication events are not yet integrated into the controlled audit-search/export surface required by the acceptance wording.

IAM-012.notes: Fresh PostgreSQL evidence proves last successful login is persisted and active sessions expose source IP, user agent, MFA verification and expiry context; /auth/me and /auth/sessions expose the corresponding current-user views.

IAM-013.notes: Authorised administration can revoke all sessions for a user; fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves the revoked token fails immediately.

IAM-014.notes: Human account provisioning rejects generic/shared-account naming patterns and automated actions can use attributable non-login/service identities. Complete production evidence that every activity maps to a unique human or scoped service identity remains deployment-dependent.

IAM-015.notes: Database bootstrap defines separate NOLOGIN least-privilege roles for control API and individual worker classes and explicitly avoids committed credentials. Actual production credential review proving distinct rotatable LOGIN identities and no shared superuser secret remains an infrastructure/deployment gate.

IAM-016.notes: IP/CIDR admission is deployment-configurable, trusted-proxy handling is explicit, spoofed forwarding is rejected, and requests outside the configured allowlist receive NETWORK_ACCESS_DENIED while health endpoints remain available.

IMP-001.notes: CSV and bounded XLSX imports run through the same protected validation/staging workflow. XLSX tests cover worksheet selection, hidden sheets, formulas and unsafe embedded/external content.

IMP-002.notes: Versioned deterministic CSV and XLSX templates are downloadable through a dedicated controlled API; unknown versions and formats fail closed.

IMP-003.notes: Reusable source mappings are governed, maker-checker approved, effective-dated and safely superseded; future replacements do not retire the current mapping before their effective boundary.

IMP-004.notes: Import intake streams to quarantine storage, enforces filename and byte limits, verifies actual CSV/XLSX signatures and records a terminal malware decision before validation can proceed.

IMP-005.notes: Dangerous spreadsheet prefixes are neutralised in import previews, row-level issue exports, CSV reports and XLSX cell rendering.

IMP-006.notes: CSV processing is streaming and production staging is bounded/durable, but the acceptance-required million-row memory-limit run has not been executed.

IMP-007.notes: PostgreSQL evidence records checksum, uploader and creation time, exact client-request replay returns the original batch, duplicate file checksum is detected, and immutable import identity fields reject direct mutation.

IMP-008.notes: Required/type validation produces row-level issue codes; invalid state/LGA relationships are quarantined distinctly while missing optional geography remains missing rather than invented.

IMP-009.notes: MSISDN normalisation supports explicit international numbers and governed country rules; a national number without an explicit recognised country is rejected rather than guessed.

IMP-010.notes: Durable PostgreSQL staging ranks duplicate lookup HMACs, keeps one canonical staged row, records DUPLICATE_MSISDN issues for later rows and reconciles duplicate counts; preview also detects duplicates before commit.

IMP-011.notes: Merge distinguishes inserted and updated canonical contacts and preserves source lineage, but there is no first-class unchanged/no-change contact count, so insert/update/no-change cannot yet reconcile exactly as required.

IMP-012.notes: Fill-null, newest-source, trusted-source and manual-conflict policies are implemented; manual conflicts support governed single and atomic batch decisions with optimistic versions.

IMP-013.notes: A profile import cannot silently broaden consent: PostgreSQL profile updates preserve withdrawn consent, merge requires approved clean consent evidence, and import-derived grants are scoped and recorded with transactional consent events.

IMP-014.notes: Preview state and cancel-before-canonical-mutation are directly proven in PostgreSQL and HTTP, with staging evidence retained. Preview does not yet estimate repository insert/update/no-change effects before commit.

IMP-015.notes: Validation/staging uses bounded batches, PostgreSQL jsonb_to_recordset, leases and restart/retry semantics; merge work is lease-fenced. No large-import throughput target and failure-recovery acceptance run has been executed.

IMP-016.notes: Authorised operators can download bounded row-level validation issues as spreadsheet-safe CSV with masked identifiers and auditable search/export evidence.

IMP-017.notes: Uploaded, valid, invalid, duplicate, suppressed, inserted and updated totals are persisted/reconciled and conflicts can be closed with immutable evidence. A distinct unchanged-contact count is still outstanding, so exact row-total reconciliation is incomplete.

IMP-018.notes: Direct PostgreSQL evidence proves rollback rejects an older import after a later independent source, while rolling back the newer import restores prior profile/source lineage, preserves prior active consent, revokes only import-derived consent and records append-only rollback evidence.

IMP-019.notes: PostgreSQL merge rejects a batch whose consent review is not approved, and the legacy snapshot endpoint no longer trusts caller-supplied members: it derives membership server-side through governed cohort eligibility. An unapproved batch therefore cannot enter canonical audience membership or bypass the snapshot gate.

IMP-020.notes: Secure intake derives source expiry from configured retention duration when not supplied internally; lease-fenced deletion removes expired terminal import objects and records append-only success/failure evidence with hashed object keys.

MET-001.notes: Backend dashboard/report data exists for audience, delivery, engagement, exceptions and operations, but no frontend large-campaign dashboard NFR timing evidence proves the acceptance target.

MET-002.notes: Import reconciliation covers uploaded, valid, invalid, duplicate and suppressed rows with balanced totals, but the required consent-ineligible, capped and final-eligible waterfall is not represented end-to-end.

MET-003.notes: The recipient ledger has the required delivery states, but campaign aggregate/report output collapses CLAIMED into queued and GATEWAY_ACCEPTED into submitted and does not expose cancelled as a distinct aggregate.

MET-004.notes: Report terminology directly keeps submitted and delivered distinct, but frontend/UI terminology evidence is deferred and therefore the combined UI/report acceptance is not fully closed.

MET-005.notes: No report/dashboard model was found that exposes a denominator and formula definition for every rate in hover/export form.

MET-006.notes: No campaign report/dashboard implementation was found for current, average and peak submission throughput reconciled to event/time-bucket data.

MET-007.notes: Queue depth and oldest queued job evidence exist and execution forecasts react to measured throughput changes, but they are not proven as one campaign dashboard view refreshing at a governed/configured interval.

MET-008.notes: Campaign report exposes actual execution start and completion timestamps, but it does not expose completion-deadline variance as a report field.

MET-009.notes: Retry attempts and failure details are durable, but campaign report/dashboard does not yet aggregate retry count, retry rate and major failure reasons with attempt reconciliation.

MET-010.notes: Campaign pool report exposes sender-pool allocation and delivery/failure/unknown counts, but success ratio, latency and reconnect count roll-ups required by the acceptance are missing.

MET-011.notes: State/LGA/gender/age breakdowns reconcile to campaign recipient membership in PostgreSQL, including UNKNOWN buckets, but the SQL reads current contact attributes rather than frozen snapshot attributes; historical/as-of demographic reporting is therefore not closed.

MET-012.notes: Minimum cohort thresholds are governed and versioned. PostgreSQL report evidence proves a threshold of two leaves Lagos=2 visible while all one-person demographic/geographic cells are suppressed and raw breakdowns do not escape the reporting boundary.

MET-013.notes: Opt-out counts are reported and inbound/reply handling exists elsewhere, but link-click collection is not implemented and report metric definitions do not explicitly document collection limitations.

MET-014.notes: Delivery transitions update campaign_metrics incrementally inside the same PostgreSQL transaction, avoiding recipient rescans for core counters. The acceptance additionally requires a bounded-query-plan performance test, which is not yet present.

MET-015.notes: A PostgreSQL replay test proves an identical delivery event is stored once and does not apply a second metric delta; queued/submitted counters remain unchanged on replay.

MET-016.notes: No evidence currently proves configurable near-real-time campaign dashboard refresh or that update latency meets the stated NFR.

MET-017.notes: An authorised user can request an organisation-facing campaign report, a separate checker approves/freeze-snapshots it, and the export worker renders it for short-lived retrieval without portal access.

MET-018.notes: CSV, PDF and XLSX renderers produce structurally valid files. A direct regression proves the same delivered total survives all three report formats.

MET-019.notes: A PostgreSQL-backed report-content security test injects campaign internal notes, organisation internal notes, raw provider error detail and an unnecessary MSISDN-like value and proves none appear in JSON or CSV client report output.

MET-020.notes: Export requests record template version and support watermark/caveat-like warning content, but no governed approved-branding model/approval evidence was found.

MET-021.notes: Campaign/report data is retained and terminal campaigns can be archived without deleting authoritative rows, but archived-report regeneration from retained summary data is not directly proven and current demographic breakdowns depend on mutable contact attributes.

MET-022.notes: Export records contain request/approval actors, template version, generated time and output SHA-256, but the completing worker/generator identity is not retained as a complete report audit field and no acceptance-level complete-audit-record test exists.

MET-023.notes: No campaign recipient-level exception export matching the permissioned, encrypted, logged and masked acceptance was found in the active implementation.

MET-024.notes: Reports warn when campaign metrics are unavailable and when UNKNOWN outcomes require reconciliation, preventing some false-completeness claims. Metric reconciliation drift is detected/recorded but is not surfaced in the campaign report, so reconciliation-gap quality flags are incomplete.

ORG-001.notes: Internal organisation records are created and used by campaign governance without external portal-user credentials. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves the persistent organisation aggregate is independently usable by the campaign service.

ORG-002.notes: Legal/trading name, country and status are active model/repository fields and legal-name/email/country-format validation exists. Schema also has registration_reference and industry, but the active organisation model/API/repository does not read or write those fields, so the required record is incomplete.

ORG-003.notes: The current organisation aggregate has only one primary contact name/email. No first-class multiple internal/external organisation-contact model with role, communication details and active/effective dating was found.

ORG-004.notes: A controller_role column exists on organisations but is not wired through the active organisation model/repository/API. Consent-review evidence separately records and validates controller role, so campaign consent evidence can carry the role, but it is not yet governed as an organisation-level attribute.

ORG-005.notes: Versioned maker-checker organisation policy governs allowed/prohibited campaign purposes. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance activates the policy and proves a prohibited purpose is rejected by campaign creation while an allowed purpose proceeds.

ORG-006.notes: ACTIVE, SUSPENDED, UNDER_REVIEW and CLOSED are explicit lifecycle states.
