Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves status transitions persist with actor evidence and a suspended organisation is rejected by campaign creation; campaign progression and final dispatch also require the organisation to remain ACTIVE.

ORG-007.notes: Campaign commercial records capture quotation/invoice/payment/currency/recipient entitlement and use maker-checker approval. PostgreSQL persistence is exercised and campaign release governance can require the approved campaign-specific commercial entitlement.

ORG-008.notes: Versioned organisation events persist actor, reason, event type and before/after status and are retrievable; fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves that path. Ordinary profile updates do not persist the previous legal/trading/country/contact values, so full historical values cannot be reconstructed from organisation history.

ORG-009.notes: Normalised legal-name plus country duplicate protection exists in memory and PostgreSQL; fresh acceptance proves a normalised duplicate is rejected. The SRS calls for a potential-duplicate warning based on configured identifiers, while current behavior is a fixed hard rejection with no configurable identifier/warning workflow.

ORG-010.notes: Approved, versioned and effective-dated organisation policy stores contact/campaign retention and report brand/footer settings. No report-generation path was found that consumes those approved branding fields and records the exact policy version used, so the acceptance is not fully met.

PRV-001.notes: Privacy cases normalise a complete E.164 subject, derive the protected lookup HMAC and resolve the canonical contact without partial plaintext search. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves a known number maps to the expected contact ID while the externally visible subject remains masked; plaintext decryption is confined to approved package execution.

PRV-002.notes: Approved access cases encrypt a subject package containing the current profile/source fields, attribute source data, consent, suppressions and campaign history. However the package model/query does not expose the separate contact_sources provenance/history records maintained by imports, so the exact SRS requirement for profile, sources, consent, suppression and campaign history is not fully closed.

PRV-003.notes: Approved rectification allows only governed fields and preserves the complete pre-change profile with privacy case, actor, reason and original source provenance. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves the current value changes while attributed history remains intact.

PRV-004.notes: Approved objection execution atomically marks the contact SUPPRESSED and creates one effective GLOBAL WHATSAPP suppression on the subject lookup HMAC. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves that mutation, while final-dispatch PostgreSQL acceptance independently proves active suppression/contact ineligibility blocks future sends.

PRV-005.notes: Erasure is blocked by active legal hold, removes unnecessary attributes/profile PII, withdraws active consent, replaces the encrypted MSISDN payload, marks the contact ANONYMISED/restricted, preserves the lookup HMAC and creates a minimised global suppression. PostgreSQL acceptance proves the original PII is removed while suppression identity and the completed decision record remain.

PRV-006.notes: Approved portability/access execution creates an encrypted structured package with integrity hash. Fresh PostgreSQL acceptance proves ExportEnvelope appends the authoritative EXPORT_REQUESTED event; the delivery path is actor-bound, expiring, single-use and audited, and the HTTP route enforces privacy permission plus recent MFA step-up.

PRV-007.notes: Privacy cases persist status, requested/due times, assignee/owner and immutable lifecycle evidence, with indexes for open-case due-date queries. No backend worker/alert policy currently produces an overdue DSAR alert, so the exact acceptance remains incomplete.

PRV-008.notes: Disclosure-producing access/portability cases require submission, independent approval and a separate executor; maker cannot approve and checker cannot execute their own decision. Ordinary case JSON excludes encrypted result material, and controlled export additionally requires permission and recent MFA step-up, providing the required review gate before release.

PRV-009.notes: Legal holds use draft, submission, independent approval/rejection, active and release states with immutable reasoned events. Fresh PostgreSQL retention acceptance proves scheduled privacy-case deletion excludes an otherwise-due case under an active hold. The scheduler currently filters held records silently and does not append a dedicated skip/hold reason for that deletion decision, so the exact logging portion remains incomplete.

PRV-010.notes: No first-class privacy-impact/data-inventory report currently identifies the required data categories, processing purposes, source provenance and retention policy in one governed report.

REP-001.notes: The authoritative checkout is local/bundle-backed and the connected GitHub installation exposes no matching hosted campaign-platform repository. Private visibility and approved-organisation-member access therefore cannot yet be evidenced.

REP-002.notes: The repository retains the proprietary root notice, OpenWA third-party notice, provenance record and original MIT licence in the vendored source. No automated release-artifact packaging/verification step was found that proves these files are present in every release artefact, so the exact acceptance remains open.

REP-003.notes: The exact upstream URL, supplied archive name/version, archive SHA-256 and import/review date are recorded. The imported archive has no .git metadata and the exact upstream Git commit is explicitly UNVERIFIED, so the required commit SHA/build-baseline identity is incomplete.

REP-004.notes: Policy explicitly treats public OpenWA upstream as read-only, untrusted input and prohibits automatic merge/deployment; the checkout has no public-upstream Git remote and CI has no upstream fetch/merge job. This is documented/structural evidence rather than an enforced hosted remote policy, so the row remains partial.

REP-005.notes: The documented update model requires manual import into an isolated review branch followed by provenance/security review, tests and internal review, and CI runs on pull requests. No tracked upstream-fetch workflow or hosted branch-rule evidence proves an upstream update can only reach main through that controlled review path.

REP-006.notes: No matching hosted repository is visible through the connected GitHub installation, so organisation/repository fork restrictions cannot be evidenced from either the checkout or hosted settings.

REP-007.notes: CI exists for pull requests and main pushes, but branch-protection rules blocking direct/force push and unreviewed merges are hosted repository settings and no matching hosted repository is available to verify them.

REP-008.notes: No CODEOWNERS file is committed and no hosted test pull request/required code-owner rule is available to demonstrate enforced approval for gateway, security, database and infrastructure changes.

REP-009.notes: Deployed Node applications have lockfiles and production Compose requires image values to be digest-pinned at deployment. The root package has no package-lock.json, production image digests are supplied externally rather than committed, CI actions use floating major tags, and strict SBOM verification currently fails on the missing root lockfile.

REP-010.notes: A deterministic CycloneDX generator exists and the normal release-security gate freshly produced a 30-component SBOM. CI invokes that gate, but the workflow does not upload/retain the generated SBOM as a release artefact and artifacts/sbom.cdx.json is not tracked, so release retention is not proven.

REP-011.notes: Fresh normal release-security validation passed production-compose structure, committed-secret scanning and npm dependency audits with no production exceptions. gitleaks/Trivy/Syft are available only behind STRICT_RELEASE_SECURITY and normal CI does not enable that mode or perform a release image vulnerability scan, so the full source/dependency/secret/image gate is incomplete.

REP-012.notes: The repository contains no first-party Dependabot/Renovate/upstream auto-merge or deployment workflow; upstream policy explicitly requires manual review and CI checks. Hosted required-review and staging-approval enforcement is not evidenced, so the exact all-updates acceptance remains partial.

SEG-001.notes: Backend filter/cohort validation, compilation and estimate/materialisation APIs exist, but the required visual no-SQL segment-builder UI is deferred with the frontend programme.

SEG-002.notes: Equality, inclusion/exclusion, range and known/unknown operators are implemented and tested, but there is no true relative-recency operator.

SEG-003.notes: Core catalogue covers country/state/LGA, reported age, gender, language and consent purpose, with governed dynamic typed attributes for extensibility. A first-class source filter and distinct consent-status attributes are not implemented.

SEG-004.notes: Fresh PostgreSQL evidence proves reported-age 18..35 is inclusive (17/36 excluded, 18/35 included) and demographic match without consent is excluded. The estimated-age policy/model required by the full requirement is absent.

SEG-005.notes: Reported age retains collection date/source and verification metadata, but there is no derived estimated-age method or general confidence model and the operator-facing display remains deferred with the frontend.

SEG-006.notes: AGE_RECORDED_AT is filterable as a date, but there is no governed configurable age-staleness period/policy and no separate stale-record count as required.

SEG-007.notes: Fresh PostgreSQL cohort evidence proves a demographic match without active matching organisation/purpose/channel consent is excluded; consent is part of the authoritative eligibility query.

SEG-008.notes: Suppression, active contact state and governed frequency caps are enforced in cohort/final eligibility, but the acceptance criterion also requires a reconciled count waterfall, which is not implemented end-to-end.

SEG-009.notes: Fresh tests prove nested AND/OR, rejection beyond depth/rule bounds and SQL-field injection resistance. The complexity bounds are code constants (depth 5/rules 50), not governed/configurable as required.

SEG-010.notes: No implementation was found that renders an accurate human-readable summary of nested segment logic.

SEG-011.notes: Cohort estimates return only aggregate eligible count and calculation time without MSISDNs/identities. Required estimate latency/NFR evidence has not been produced.

SEG-012.notes: Individual demographic/consent/suppression/cap/final-eligibility controls exist, but there is no single reconciled demographic -> consent -> expiry -> suppression -> cap -> final-eligible count waterfall tied to the snapshot.

SEG-013.notes: Segment definitions support create/update version history, clone, archive/retire and version comparison; version rows and frozen snapshot references preserve historical definition evidence.

SEG-014.notes: Sensitive fields are hidden/rejected through permission-aware registry validation and compilation, including direct backend submission. No distinct governed data-use-policy layer restricting segment fields was found.

SEG-015.notes: Snapshot hash commits definition/policy/configuration evidence. A fresh RED->GREEN PostgreSQL test proved that before migration 0071 frozen membership accepted UPDATE/DELETE/extra INSERT, while 0071 rejects all three and preserves the frozen member count.

SEG-016.notes: Snapshot persistence stores creation time, definition version, consent/configuration policy versions and initiating user. The API does not expose a complete dedicated snapshot audit/read view containing all required evidence.

SEG-017.notes: Fresh PostgreSQL final-eligibility tests prove queued recipients are rechecked for matching consent/suppression and other safety boundaries immediately before dispatch, so post-snapshot withdrawal/opt-out is excluded.

SEG-018.notes: Snapshot overlap analysis returns intersection, left-only, right-only and union counts without returning contact identities.

SEG-019.notes: A configurable, governed minimum-cohort policy suppresses small demographic/geographic cells in campaign/organisation reports. Equivalent enforcement is not yet applied to cohort estimates/segment previews or a segment dashboard boundary.

SEG-020.notes: Asynchronous materialisation has durable progress, bounded pages, fenced lease/reclaim, restart-safe checkpoints and duplicate-safe final snapshot commit, including PostgreSQL evidence. The acceptance workload has not been demonstrated at multi-million audience scale.

SND-001.notes: A governed PostgreSQL sender inventory exists with controlled account metadata and masked identity, and the embedded gateway maintains session records. Genuine WhatsApp-account/MSISDN evidence has not been established with real paired accounts, so the genuine-account requirement remains externally unproven.

SND-002.notes: A PostgreSQL-backed HTTP test proves plaintext E.164 is AES-GCM encrypted before persistence, only the masked value is returned by create/read models, ciphertext does not equal plaintext, and decrypting the stored ciphertext recovers the original number.

SND-003.notes: New sender sessions require ownership, registration-country, display-name and non-secret recovery-reference metadata. Existing installations remain upgrade-safe through nullable migration columns and can be completed through an MFA-protected optimistic update. Recovery references are write-only and suppressed from ordinary sender JSON and audit evidence; live PostgreSQL tests prove persistence, audit and masking.

SND-004.notes: Logical sender pools map to governed concrete sessions. PostgreSQL allocation evidence proves a recipient obligation is assigned to the actual eligible sender session selected from its logical pool. Multi-pool plans deterministically bind shards to approved pools and retain immutable reallocation evidence.

SND-005.notes: The deferred production UI/help/reporting acceptance has not yet proven clear disclosure that a logical sender is not an alphanumeric WhatsApp sender ID.

SND-006.notes: The canonical sender lifecycle is enforced before gateway side effects. Allocation requires eligible READY/BUSY sender state plus a READY non-draining owner node, fresh heartbeats and a live lease; PostgreSQL evidence proves stale/expired ownership is excluded.

SND-007.notes: Accepted lease tranche ee79e82 proves one boot-bound owner across signed heartbeat, PostgreSQL lease/session atomicity, allocation/materialisation and gateway current-process ownership. Exact Linux/PostgreSQL/race/build gates and blind review accepted the tranche; stale/current-boot conflicts are fenced before activation or provider submission.

SND-008.notes: Accepted lease tranche ee79e82 uses the shared bounded SENDER_HEARTBEAT_TTL for heartbeat ownership, allocation and capacity. PostgreSQL and memory evidence prove renewal, expiry, live-lease/current-boot capacity eligibility and fencing-history preservation.

SND-009.notes: Accepted lease tranche ee79e82 proves a new boot cannot steal a live lease or become READY/BUSY directly after expiry. Recovery must first establish non-sending ownership; gateway engines retire on ownership loss and reconnect only after current-process ownership is re-established.

SND-010.notes: The node inventory records internal/public network identity, pool, provider, engine, boot and deployed versions. Hostinger/VPS inventory reconciliation remains an external deployment control.

SND-011.notes: The embedded gateway enforces a configured maximum concurrent-session ceiling and the test suite proves excess session start is rejected. Container resource telemetry is also captured, but admission does not currently use CPU/memory/disk/inode evidence or a tested VPS resource model. Resource-aware multi-session placement therefore remains partial.

SND-012.notes: Per-session HTTP/HTTPS/SOCKS proxy configuration is encrypted with the secret keyring, versioned, audited in PostgreSQL, step-up protected for administration, and cannot be changed while the session is READY. Session start resolves the current governed proxy and passes it to the gateway; embedded-gateway tests prove proxy credentials are not persisted in the worker registry or silently reused after control-plane authority changes.

SND-013.notes: Configured safe throughput and runtime pacing are enforced. Observed-rate calibration and live engine-specific capacity evidence still require genuine OpenWA sessions.

SND-014.notes: Effective-dated maker-checker pacing policies govern per-session minimum/maximum delay, jitter, hourly and daily submission allowances, cooldown and active-campaign limits. The campaign worker enforces durable counters before provider submission.

SND-015.notes: Maker-checker SENDER.HEALTH_THRESHOLDS configuration resolves at sender-session, sender-pool, gateway-pool and platform scope with safe defaults. Health assessment uses measured failure rate, disconnect count, heartbeat recency, successful-delivery recency and capacity evidence. Threshold breach automatically drains an active sender, preventing new allocation while preserving in-flight work; live PostgreSQL integration proves the state transition, optimistic governance version and immutable service-attributed audit event. Genuine WhatsApp telemetry remains required for production calibration of threshold values, not for the implemented enforcement contract.

SND-016.notes: New sessions begin in NEW and must pass pairing, connecting and readiness transitions before allocation.

SND-017.notes: No first-class campaign- or organisation-level sender reservation workflow with conflict rejection is implemented.

SND-018.notes: MaxActiveCampaigns defaults to one when omitted. A PostgreSQL-backed pacing test proves campaign A acquires the sender, campaign B on the same sender is rejected with ErrActiveCampaignLimit, and exactly one ACTIVE sender/campaign assignment remains.

SND-019.notes: Pairing QR/code routes require sender.admin and recent MFA step-up. Direct request-level tests prove a sender.read-only user receives 403 without reaching a sensitive pairing handler, and an administrator without recent MFA is stopped by STEP_UP_REQUIRED before lifecycle/QR access.

SND-020.notes: Gateway logger tests inject a sender MSISDN, QR payload, session token, message content and credential-bearing database URL and prove the sensitive values are removed from output. The repository committed-secret scanner also passes, and embedded-gateway tests prove proxy credentials are not persisted in runtime session registry files.

SND-021.notes: Retirement is governed, fenced, blocked while active work exists and evidenced. Cryptographic or storage-level deletion of the real engine session-state volume still requires gateway/runtime implementation and live validation.

SND-022.notes: No explicit warm-standby worker/sender lifecycle exists that excludes standby capacity until a readiness health check promotes it.

UX-001.notes: The current Next.js admin shell is desktop-first/responsive with skip navigation, visible focus states, labels and semantic tables, and a fresh production build succeeds. The formal core-screen accessibility audit required by the UI/UX specification has not been run and the frontend programme remains deferred.

UX-002.notes: The shell displays an environment badge and internal-platform wording, but the badge is currently hardcoded to Development and there is no complete confidentiality/classification banner or verified production/staging differentiation.

UX-003.notes: Backend APIs default to masked identifiers and privileged reveal workflows are separately authorised, while the current frontend does not intentionally render raw MSISDNs. No production page-source/back-button acceptance proves plaintext PII is absent across all screens and authorised reveal UX is not implemented.

UX-004.notes: The campaign register displays campaign status and core timing/audience information, and backend campaign-workspace APIs expose richer warnings/next-state evidence. The current campaign UI does not consistently show owner, next required action and blocking reasons on every campaign.

UX-005.notes: The audience-builder UI has a waterfall-shaped estimate panel for profile matches, consent, suppression and final eligible counts, but it explicitly renders placeholders rather than live reconciled database counts/exclusion reasons. Backend cohort logic exists; the full progressive UX is unfinished.

UX-006.notes: The current builder supports reported-age filtering but no estimated-age method/staleness model or UI warning exists. The underlying backend estimated-age/staleness requirements are also incomplete.

UX-007.notes: Backend destructive/release/export paths use permissions, optimistic versions, reasons and MFA/maker-checker controls, preventing an unauthorised single API click from completing sensitive actions. The frontend has no comprehensive explicit confirmation dialogs for release, pause, cancel, export and override.

UX-008.notes: Backend campaign evidence freezes message/audience/consent/config-related versions, but the current admin campaign screen does not present an approval view identifying the exact immutable artefact versions.

UX-009.notes: Backend sender APIs mask actual sender MSISDNs, but the current admin-web navigation has no implemented sender page and no UI explanation of logical sender-pool behaviour.

UX-010.notes: Backend operational APIs provide queue/UNKNOWN/incidents/capacity/forecast evidence, but the current frontend dashboard is not a proven live operational campaign view with target refresh behaviour.

UX-011.notes: Backend errors carry governed reason/detail codes and the UI presents human-readable messages for some forms. There is no complete reason-code-to-remediation catalogue across operational failures, so operators may still need backend context.

UX-012.notes: No persisted personal saved-filter/view model and no frontend saved-view workflow was found.

UX-013.notes: The backend export workflow fully enforces purpose, maker-checker approval, expiry, actor-bound single-use grants, revocation and audit, so unapproved bulk export is blocked. The production frontend reports/export workflow is not implemented, so the UX requirement remains partial.

UX-014.notes: The current UI uses skip navigation, labelled controls, focus-visible styles, semantic tables/fieldsets and keyboard-operable native controls. No formal accessibility/keyboard test suite has yet passed the agreed UI/UX acceptance.

UX-015.notes: Backend sensitive responses apply anti-cache security headers and frontend campaign fetches use no-store. Browser page caching/back-button behaviour across the production admin application has not been tested, so the complete browser-facing acceptance is not closed.
